lessons.title: Planning and preparing a dispatch
lessons.html:
Dispatch is the final step

Dispatch is the process of sending packed fruit from the packhouse or cold store to the customer, port or distribution centre. Mistakes here are expensive: wrong pallets on a truck, a broken cold chain or wrong documents can lead to a rejected container overseas.

The dispatch instruction

Dispatch starts with an order or loading instruction from the marketing or logistics office. It typically states:

  • Customer or exporter, market and destination.
  • Products: fruit kind, cultivar, class, count, pack type, and the number of pallets or cartons.
  • Required temperature setting and any special protocols (for example cold treatment).
  • Vehicle or container details, loading date and time.
  • Documents needed.

Selecting the pallets

  1. Use the stock system to find pallets that match the order exactly.
  2. Apply the agreed rotation rule, normally first in, first out, unless QC directs otherwise.
  3. Check that pallets have passed inspection where required (for example PPECB export inspection) and are not on hold.
  4. Check pulp temperatures are at the required level before loading.
  5. Check pallet condition: straps tight, corner boards in place, no damaged or collapsed cartons, labels correct and readable.

Checking the vehicle or container

  • The refrigerated truck or reefer container must be clean, dry, odour-free, and free of pests.
  • Doors, seals and floor must be in good condition.
  • The refrigeration unit must be working, set to the correct temperature, and pre-cooled before loading.
  • Record the container or vehicle registration number and the set temperature.

If the vehicle or container is not acceptable, do not load. Report to the supervisor so another unit can be arranged.

lessons.title: Loading, documentation and handover
lessons.html:
Loading

  • Load from a cold loading bay where possible, with dock seals, so fruit is not exposed to heat.
  • Load quickly. Pallets should not wait on the dock.
  • Load in the sequence and positions on the load plan. Pallets must fit snugly to prevent movement, and be placed so air can circulate as the unit requires; do not block the air delivery or return.
  • Place temperature data loggers or recorders in the positions specified, and record their serial numbers.
  • Scan or record each pallet number as it is loaded, and tick it off against the order.
  • Forklifts must be operated by trained, licensed drivers. Keep people clear of the loading area.

Final checks

  1. Count pallets and cartons loaded and compare with the order.
  2. Check that no pallet is left behind and none was loaded in error.
  3. Close doors and fit the numbered seal. Record the seal number, so the receiver can confirm the load was not opened in transit.
  4. Confirm the refrigeration unit is running at the set temperature.

Documents

Typical dispatch documents include:

DocumentPurpose
Delivery note / loading listLists pallets and cartons loaded; signed by the driver
Pallet numbers and traceability detailsLinks each pallet to producer and pack date
Temperature and seal recordsProof of cold chain and security
Inspection and export documentsAs required by the exporter and market, for example inspection certificates

Documents must be accurate, complete and match the load exactly. Copies are filed for traceability.

Handover

The driver checks the load and documents and signs for them. Note any damage or discrepancies on the documents before signing. Update the stock system to show the pallets as dispatched.

Problems

If there is a shortage, wrong product, temperature problem or delay, inform the supervisor and logistics office immediately. Never hide a problem: the customer must be informed so they can plan.

Key points

  • Dispatch follows a written order or loading instruction.
  • Select correct, inspected pallets at the right pulp temperature.
  • Check the vehicle or container is clean, working and pre-cooled.
  • Load quickly, follow the load plan, place loggers and record seal numbers.
  • Documents must match the load exactly; report any discrepancy immediately.

quiz.question: What must be done to a reefer container before loading?

options.text: It must be washed with fruit wax
It must be pre-cooled to the set temperature
It must be left open in the sun
Its seal must be fitted first

quiz.question: The container smells strongly of fish. What should you do?

options.text: Do not load and report to the supervisor

quiz.question: Why is the seal number recorded?

options.text: To prove the load was not opened in transit

quiz.question: When should the driver note damage or discrepancies?
Pallets on hold or not yet inspected may be loaded if the truck is waiting.
The stock system should be updated after pallets are dispatched.
